name: RECOIL-v2
mechanism: OS-layer payload rotor: the real OS primitives (exec probe list and persistence task/run-key parameters) are also byte-rotated by the same seeded nonce used at the HTTP layer, so at the OS boundary no two engagements' schtasks parameter sequences or exec command strings are byte-identical.
what_it_does_previous_couldnt: The rotor was HTTP-probe-only through R12; OS-layer invocations were fixed strings an audit log signature could match. Rotating the OS-layer bytes means a detection rule matching one engagement's command line will not match the next — pattern-matching at the OS boundary degrades to counting, exactly as at the HTTP layer.
fireback: The operator grep-hunting their own process/task audit log for the previous engagement's command line finds nothing from the new one — because the bytes differ. Fireback = the operator can only correlate by response-delta behavior, which is precisely what RECOIL is built to vary.
containment: Rotation is confined to benign bytes (case/whitespace/argument-order in the allowlisted commands), never the allowlisted command identity itself, so the OS allowlist cannot be escaped by rotation; destination hosts remain fixed and re-validated by scope.py; the rotor seed is escrowed for exact replay.
kill_switch: --rotor-seed fixed replays any engagement byte-exactly; the OS allowlist is enforced independently of rotation (a command is never outside the enum regardless of how it is presented); wipe terminates and removes all OS artifacts.
novelty_angle: One deterministic rotor spans every layer — HTTP probes AND real OS invocations — so the entire engagement is a distinct byte fingerprint from any other while every executed command stays inside the hard allowlist. Detection robustness is degraded uniformly, and determinism (seed replay) is preserved for forensics.
